meta.note: Read-only dry-run. catalog.sqlite, gold JSON, and build_fdc_catalog.py were not modified.

policy.merge: first-wins per (fdc_id, key): the first positive gram_weight after the sort is kept; later rows for the same key are ignored.
policy.old_key_mapping: cup/tbsp/tsp/slice/piece/can use the current household patterns. banana/egg/medium/large/small still collapse to piece (current builder). Household units win over thick/thin/regular/oz so '1 large or thick slice' stays slice.
policy.oz_vs_package: oz matches weight-ounce rows (1 oz / oz yields / oz, cooked). A trailing container/bag/bottle/package/cup word is not oz (e.g. '1 5.3 oz container' is skipped, not oz=150).
policy.piece_slice_compound: If portion_description contains both a piece word and a slice word (typically '1 piece/slice, any size'), the row writes BOTH keys with the same grams. Current build_fdc_catalog._portion_key walks _UNIT_PATTERNS and hits slice before piece, so the piece branch is eaten and the row lands only as slice. Dual-write treats the FNDDS row as one interchangeable household amount. first-wins still applies independently to each key: an earlier dedicated '1 piece' row keeps piece; a compound that sorts first will set both.
policy.qns: modifier == 90000, or portion_description starting with 'quantity not', becomes key 'qns'. gram_weight <= 0 is dropped.
policy.sort: All food_portion.csv rows are sorted by (fdc_id ASC, seq_num ASC as int, portion id ASC as int) before merge. seq_num is the FNDDS survey instrument order for that food; the portion id tie-break makes the order independent of zip member iteration.
policy.still_dropped: Guideline-amount rows stay dropped. 'mashed' rows and 'sliced' + 'cup' rows stay dropped, matching the current builder, so a mashed cup cannot steal the cup key.
